children: Crude oil futures extended declines to a third consecutive session Friday, as market watchers believed the closure of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline may have a less severe impact on supply than originally feared.

While concerns remain about the Middle East war dragging on and shipping restrictions through the Strait of Hormuz, reports that the pipeline could resume partial flows within days helped oil futures pull back from four-month highs reached earlier this week.
However, repairing damaged pumping stations and fully restoring capacity could take as long as 6-8 weeks, analysts have said.

A ship-to-ship shuttle service through the strait under U.S. military protection, with oil transferred to other tankers waiting in the Gulf of Oman, reportedly could provide Saudi Arabia with another option for getting crude to buyers.

"Middle East oil flows remain surprisingly strong despite the disruption to Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline," J.P. Morgan head of global commodities strategy Natasha Kaneva said in a note, estimating total oil flows from the Middle East averaged ~17M bbl/day over the past 10 days, nearly 75% of the 2025 average.

Satellite imagery suggests the Saudis have moved 2.8M bbl/day through Hormuz over the past six days compared to just 700K bbl/day in August, the analyst said, while cautioning that the volumes could be difficult to sustain.
Meanwhile, physical premiums for oil in the North Sea, a key reference for global prices, soared to record levels Friday, after Saudi Aramco (
) told European customers they would not receive any supplies under their long-term agreements next month.

Norway's Johan Sverdrup, a grade of crude closely comparable with Saudi supplies, was offered at a premium of as much as $35/bbl above the Dated Brent physical benchmark, Bloomberg reported, after the same oil traded at a $0.60 premium less than two weeks earlier.
In the U.S., average retail prices for regular gasoline rose to $4.47/gal on Friday from $4.30 a week ago, AAA reported, while average diesel prices hit another new all-time high of $6.45/gal.
